calls.why: This is the lift I am braking hardest, and not because anything hurts. I read every note in the log by hand and there is no pain, no soreness, no tweak, no joint complaint anywhere in it — so I am not vetoing on pain and I will not pretend to. The reason is the bar itself. On 2026-08-28 you pulled 235x6, 255x5, 265x5, 265x5. On 2026-09-10, eleven days ago and the last Pull A on record, you pulled 235x5, 255x4, 255x4 — one set fewer, ten pounds lighter on top, and a rep off every set. That is the whole picture moving the wrong way at once on the only lift here that can put you on the floor for a week. A deload week exists for exactly this, so I am asking for two sets of five at 185. That is about 73% of your last top set, it is a weight you have used as a warm-up all summer, and it is unmistakably four or more reps in reserve, which is what the deload note demands. Keep the groove, spend nothing.

Straight deload math on a lift with no fatigue signal in it. On 2026-09-10 you did 88x10, 93x10, 88x9 — you went up a pin and came back down, which is a normal within-session call, not a warning. 66 lb is 30 kg, and the new gym's stacks are in kilos: your logged numbers there land on 35, 37.5, 40 and 42.5 kg exactly. I picked 66 rather than 70 because 70 is not a pin you can actually select, and I would rather you be a notch light than guessing. Two sets instead of three, per the deload set budget.

Read this one carefully, because the slot name and what you actually do have come apart. You have not done a wide cable row since the gym change — on 2026-09-10 you wrote 'One armed dumbbell row' and did four sets of 55 per hand. So I am pricing the row you actually perform, not the one the plan is still named after: 44 lb a hand, which is the 20 kg dumbbell you already used on 2026-09-15, for two sets of ten. If you do find a proper wide cable row station this week, use a weight that would be a comfortable ten with three or four left in you and stop there — do not go hunting for the old 105.

Eighty percent of the 50 you handled on 2026-09-10, two sets instead of three. One thing I will not quietly pass over: two of your three sets that day are stamped 2026-09-10 15:45:20 and 2026-09-10 15:45:21 — one and a bit seconds apart. Those two were typed in together after the fact, not timed as they happened. I am still using them, because a recalled ten at 50 is still a ten at 50, but nobody on this panel should treat that session's set-by-set detail as measured.

This lift has been the steadiest thing on the day: 35 lb on 2026-08-18, 35 on 2026-08-28, 35 on 2026-09-10, with reps sitting around eleven and twelve every time. Nothing is wrong with it, which is why it gets the plain deload treatment and nothing more — 27.5 is eighty percent of 35, two sets instead of three.

I am writing the numbers down here specifically so nobody shaves this one. The deload's set budget, applied blindly, turns your two sets into one, and cutting the only shoulder-health work on the day during the week set aside for recovery is backwards. Two sets at 27.5 for thirteen costs you nothing to recover from — that is exactly what you did on 2026-09-10 and again on 2026-09-15 — and it is the only external rotation and only back-of-the-shoulder work on Pull A. You asked on 2026-08-28 why it was three and said you thought two was right; you got two, and two is what I am defending. Same weight, same reps, no cut.

vetoes.why: Advisory, and aimed at the head coach rather than at you. I am on record against any Pull A deadlift prescription this week that asks for more than two sets or for more than 185 on the bar. You already voted with your own hands eleven days ago: the plan asked four sets and you did three, and the top weight came down from 265 to 255 with a rep missing off each one. The last lower-body session in between, 2026-09-17, cannot settle the question either way — twenty-one sets are stamped inside twenty-three minutes, three RDL sets six seconds apart, so that file is a recollection, not a measurement. When the evidence is a regression plus an unreadable session, the deload week takes the conservative side.
